message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: Livepatch documentation

on:
  push:
    paths:
      - .github/workflows/livepatch-docs.yml
      - docs/os/livepatches/**
      - skills/manage-livepatch/**
      - mkdocs.yml
      - Makefile
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - .github/workflows/livepatch-docs.yml
      - docs/os/livepatches/**
      - skills/manage-livepatch/**
      - mkdocs.yml
      - Makefile

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  documentation:
    name: Check livepatch documentation
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: cachix/install-nix-action@v31.11.5

      - name: Cache Nix store
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: /nix/store
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-nix-${{ hashFiles('flake.lock', 'flake.nix') }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ runner.os }}-nix-

      - name: Build documentation strictly
        run: nix develop .#vpsadminos --command mkdocs build --strict

      - name: Check livepatch skill routes
        run: |
          grep -Fq '(../../docs/os/livepatches/process.md)' skills/manage-livepatch/SKILL.md
          grep -Fq '(../../docs/os/livepatches/template.md)' skills/manage-livepatch/SKILL.md
",
  "rationale": "The workflow uses Nix to build documentation via `nix develop .#vpsadminos --command mkdocs build --strict`. Each run downloads or builds Nix dependencies into `/nix/store` on a fresh runner. Adding a GitHub Actions cache step for the Nix store, keyed by the flake lockfile (`flake.lock`) and flake definition (`flake.nix`), avoids repeated dependency fetching on subsequent runs. This follows the P-LIT-GHA-CACHE pattern (cache dependency downloads) demonstrated in experiment:batch-interactive-three--91c08fe132959200, which showed ~20% elapsed-time savings for Gradle dependency caching. The Nix store is immutable and content-addressed, satisfying the pattern's safety requirements. The cache is inserted after Nix installation and before the build step, preserving all existing build and test coverage.",
  "evidence_ids": ["experiment:batch-interactive-three--91c08fe132959200"]
}
